subject: Computer Networking
title: Canary Deployments
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Canary Deployments.

hook.text: Test a change on 1% of servers before rolling it to all. That's a canary deployment.

buildup.text: Named after canaries in coal mines, canary deploys expose a small group to a change first and monitor results.

discovery.text: If the canary group shows errors, rollout stops automatically. Blast radius stays tiny, not global.

twist.text: Many major outages could have been prevented by canary deploys. The change would have failed small, not big.

climax.text: Facebook now uses staged rollouts after their 2021 BGP meltdown. CrowdStrike committed to canaries after 2024.

punchline.text: Deploy to a few first. If they survive, deploy to all.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of a canary deployment?
options: To test changes on a small group before a full rollout
To deploy updates as fast as possible
To roll back all changes automatically

details.summary: Canary deployments roll out changes to a small percentage of servers first, monitor for problems, then gradually expand. Named after canaries in coal mines, this strategy catches dangerous changes before they affect all users.
details.whyItMatters: Canary deployments are the single most effective practice for preventing configuration and code changes from causing global outages.
takeaways: Deploy changes to a small subset of servers first
Monitor error rates and performance before expanding
Automatic rollback on anomaly detection prevents cascading failure

faq.question: How does a canary deployment work in practice?
faq.answer: A change is deployed to one or two percent of servers. Automated monitoring compares error rates, latency, and resource usage against the unchanged servers. If metrics stay healthy, the rollout expands gradually. If anomalies are detected, the change is automatically rolled back.

faq.question: Why don't all companies use canary deployments?
faq.answer: They require sophisticated monitoring, automated comparison, and rollback infrastructure. Small organizations may lack the tooling. Some changes like database schema migrations are difficult to canary. But for most code and configuration changes, canaries are straightforward and effective.
